title: Mechanical Engineer
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.
Location: Glasgow, UK (on-site)
Travel: Minimal
The Role
We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design and develop the mechanical systems that make up our robotic synthesis platform — the fluidic handling, motion assemblies, enclosures, and instrument modules that physically carry out chemistry. You will take designs from concept through detailed CAD, prototyping, and testing into production, working closely with electronics, firmware, and manufacturing engineers.
What sets this role apart is that your designs do not just move — they handle real reagents and run real chemistry, so precision, reliability, and material compatibility matter as much as elegant mechanics.
If designing mechanical systems for a real-world robotic platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
- Design mechanical assemblies and components — motion systems, fluidics, fixtures, and enclosures — from concept to production.
- Produce detailed 3D CAD models, drawings, and tolerance analyses.
- Prototype, test, and iterate hardware, validating designs against real-world performance.
- Partner with electronics and firmware engineers on integrated electromechanical modules.
- Work with manufacturing and supply chain on design-for-manufacture, materials, and component selection.
- Contribute to design reviews and the team’s mechanical standards. About You
You are a hands-on mechanical engineer who enjoys taking a design from sketch to working hardware. You sweat the details — tolerances, materials, manufacturability — and you like seeing your parts come together and move in the real world.
We expect you to bring:
- Proven experience in mechanical design engineering, ideally for precision electromechanical or robotic hardware.
- Strong CAD skills (e.g. SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) and detailed drawing / GD&T experience.
- Sound grasp of mechanisms, materials, tolerancing, and design-for-manufacture.
- Hands-on prototyping and testing experience.
- Close collaboration with electronics, firmware, and manufacturing engineers. Beneficial Skills
- Experience with fluidics, pumps, valves, or motion systems.
- Exposure to lab instrumentation, robotics, or automation hardware.
- Familiarity with manufacturing processes (machining, sheet metal, injection moulding, 3D printing).
- FEA or tolerance-stack analysis.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact.   The mechanical systems you design are the body of our platform — your work is what physically carries out chemistry in the Chemifarm.
Autonomy.   You will own mechanical design across modules and shape how our hardware is built.
Ambition.   We are a Series B deep-tech company at the frontier of chemistry, robotics, and AI — with the resources and mandate to design mechanical systems for a platform unlike anything else.

title: Senior Software Engineer
text:
Location: Glasgow • Workstyle: Hybrid • Reports to : VP Software Engineering

About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world's largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
The Role
Everything Chemify does runs on the Unified Data Platform. When a molecule is designed, registered, sourced, synthesised by a robot, tested, and shipped, the platform is what carries it, one canonical identity for every chemical entity, one trusted answer for its properties and hazards, one record of what was actually made and shipped to clients.
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to own crucial parts of that platform. This is a genuinely full-stack role: you'll own applications end-to-end, the interfaces chemists and operations staff use every day, the services behind them, and the data pipelines that feed them.
The platform spans seven domains, chemical identity and registration, chemical safety, inventory, sourcing, reaction data, reference data, and the shared infrastructure underneath. You won't work across all of it, but you won't be boxed into one corner either. We'll match your area to your strengths and appetite, and we expect that to change as the platform grows. What stays constant is the level of ownership: your systems, your architecture calls, your users.
You'll work in a tight-knit, cross-functional environment spanning software, chemistry, operations, and programme management, the kind of place where curiosity across disciplines is an asset, not a distraction.
If you enjoy solving complex technical problems that make a real-world impact, are a natural communicator, and are energised by working closely with scientists using cutting-edge technology, we'd love to hear from you.
What You'll Work On
Applications people rely on daily. Full ownership of user-facing systems used by chemists, analysts, and operations teams across multiple sites, from the interface through to the data model.
Services that are the single source of truth. Registration and reference services where being authoritative matters, and where every other system is a consumer with its own expectations.
Domain modelling that has to be right. Chemical entities, batches, lineage, properties, hazards. These are hard models with real edge cases, and the abstractions you choose will outlive the code.
Data pipelines and orchestration. Dagster pipelines feeding a versioned data lake and a warehouse serving multiple use cases, with the reproducibility and governance that scientific data demands.
Reconciling sources that disagree. External datasets, vendor systems, and instruments that each claim a different truth, promoting trusted values into the systems everyone else depends on.
Key Responsibilities
- Own the full lifecycle of the applications and services in your area: scoping, architecture, development, deployment, and monitoring production.
- Design data models and workflows covering a wide range of use cases across AI chemistry, synthesis, and manufacturing.
- Build and maintain robust, observable pipelines for internal, client-specific, and literature data.
- Work directly with chemists and operations staff to understand how the work actually happens, not how the spec says it happens.
- Collaborate with Infrastructure to ensure new work is soundly architected and production-ready.
- Define and champion engineering and data best practices: versioning, testing, documentation, governance, data contracts.
- Mentor engineers and contribute to communities of practice across the team.
- Contribute to team-wide initiatives: code reviews, design discussions, ADRs, process improvements, and workstream planning.
What You'll Bring
Core
- Significant commercial software engineering experience.
- Strong Python, with production experience in FastAPI, Django, Flask, or similar.
- PostgreSQL fluency, schema design, query optimisation, and ORM frameworks such as SQLAlchemy/SQLModel.
- Commercial experience with TypeScript and React, and a genuine interest in UI/UX.
- Experience building and maintaining data-intensive applications, you're comfortable on both sides of the application/data boundary.
- Comfortable with containerised deployments (Docker) and CI/CD pipelines (GitLab, ArgoCD).
- Hands-on with AWS or another major cloud platform.
- Experience integrating with systems you don't own, negotiating contracts, handling partial failure, and enabling teams to own their data.
- You've genuinely rewired how you work around AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or equivalent), this is part of how we work, not a nice-to-have.
- Strong communicator, genuinely collaborative, comfortable with non-technical domain experts as your primary users.
Infrastructure & Data
- Working knowledge of Kubernetes/EKS, comfortable deploying to and reasoning about containerised workloads in a managed K8s environment.
- Experience orchestrating pipelines with Dagster, Airflow, Prefect, or similar.
- Solid grasp of ETL concepts and production-grade pipeline design.
​ Beneficial Skills
- Interest in chemistry, life sciences, robotics, or manufacturing.
- Hands-on experience with scientific data, chemical, biological, or laboratory.
- Experience building systems where the data model represents physical things, and being out of sync with reality has consequences.
- Previous experience in AI drug discovery is a genuine differentiator for us.
- Interest in semantic technologies (graph databases, ontologies) or modern data stack.
- Experience enabling analytics teams by building data models for BI tools and dashboards.
- Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (AWS CDK or Terraform) is a strong plus.
- Experience with product design thinking and tools such as Figma.
- A degree in Computer Science, a scientific discipline, or a related field, useful, not required. We care what you've built.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact: You'll own foundational parts of the platform that every other team at Chemify builds on, accelerating discovery and unlocking new possibilities in science and medicine.
Ownership: Real architectural authority over systems that matter, not tickets from someone else's backlog.
Autonomy: Reporting to the VP Software Engineering, you'll have genuine influence over technical direction and product quality.
Ambition: Series B, scaling rapidly, tackling problems at the frontier of robotics, AI, and chemistry. We're building the right foundations for the future.

title: Synthetic Chemist
text:
Analysis review scientist – NMR & UPLC-MS interpretation
About Chemify
Chemify is creating a future where important molecules, drugs and currently unimaginable new materials are instantly accessible; thereby radically increasing the speed of innovation, quality of life, and reach of humanity. The company is building the infrastructure to digitize chemistry for the design, discovery and synthesis of new molecules with the desired function and properties instantly and on-demand. Chemify has built a platform that combines purpose-built programming languages, robotics, AI, and the world's largest and continuously growing database of chemical programs to accelerate chemical discovery to new, transformative heights.
Chemify is supported by some of the best investors from Silicon Valley and across the world, including Triatomic Capital, BlueYard Ventures, DCVC, Founders Fund, and others.
What we offer
You'll join our analysis review team interpreting 1H-NMR and UPLC-MS data generated by our automated synthesis platform, playing a direct and critical role in keeping our chemistry pipeline moving. You'll also get exposure to a wide variety of organic chemistry reactions passing through the platform — genuinely interesting territory if you enjoy the puzzle of structure elucidation. This is an entry point into the synthetic chemistry industry, with full training provided. Working a shift pattern that includes evenings and weekends, you'll also earn a competitive uplift for unsocial hours on top of your base salary.
Job purpose
As our Analysis Review Scientist, you will review and interpret 1H-NMR and UPLC-MS data produced by our automated chemistry platform, confirming that reactions and purifications have produced the expected outcome, flagging anomalies for further investigation, and generating high-quality reports. This is a computer-based role, working with digital spectra and data files rather than at the bench. The role follows a structured, repeatable process across a high volume of samples each shift, and forms part of a rota that includes evenings and weekends to keep pace with round-the-clock synthesis.
Who we are looking for
We're looking for an entry-level scientist — ideal for a recent chemistry graduate or someone early in their career — who is comfortable with focused, detail-oriented work performed to a consistent standard. You'll have a working knowledge of 1H-NMR and mass spectrometry from your studies or lab experience, a methodical approach to spotting when something doesn't match expectations, and the flexibility to work a rota that includes evenings and weekends. Strong communication matters too: you'll work closely with our synthesis program manager team on interpreting outcomes, and may occasionally liaise with the operations team when troubleshooting instrument or pipeline issues.
Key responsibilities
• Data interpretation: Review 1H-NMR spectra and UPLC-MS traces against expected reaction and purification outcomes, confirming success or diagnosing likely products and where a reaction may have gone wrong, to help inform future runs.
• Volume and turnaround: Process a high throughput of samples each shift to keep pace with the automated synthesis platform, maintaining consistent accuracy and speed.
• Shift coverage: Work a rota that includes evenings and weekends, providing near-continuous data turnaround for the chemistry team.
• Escalation: Flag ambiguous or unexpected spectra to senior scientists for further review, and report issues with the software platform or automated processing and verification steps.
• Record keeping: Maintain accurate, consistent records of interpretations and decisions in line with SOPs.
• Quality and compliance: Follow SOPs and quality procedures for data review and support timely investigation of flagged discrepancies or audit findings.
• Continuous improvement: Feedback patterns or recurring issues you spot to help refine interpretation guidelines over time, collaborating cross-functionally in line with one of Chemify's core values.
Qualifications and experience
Essential
• Education: PhD in synthetic chemistry, or equivalent experience — no prior industry experience required
• Technical grounding: Working knowledge of LC/HPLC/UPLC data, including mass spectrometry and UV/Vis and/or ELSD detection, gained through study or lab work
• NMR experience: Experience interpreting 1H-NMR data, with some basic structure elucidation experience expected
• Organic chemistry knowledge: A solid understanding of organic chemistry, to make sense of the reactions under review and anticipate likely side products or impurities
• Working style: Comfortable with repetitive, detail-oriented work carried out to a consistent standard
• Flexibility: Able to work a rotating shift pattern that includes evenings and weekends
• Communication: Good written and verbal communication, both for recording findings clearly and discussing reaction outcomes with senior scientists
Desired (not essential)
• 2D NMR interpretation: Experience interpreting 2D NMR data (e.g. COSY, HSQC, HMBC) for more complex structure elucidation
• Software: Experience with MestreNova or similar NMR processing software — full training will be provided if not
Compensation and working pattern
A competitive base salary, plus an uplift for unsocial hours worked as part of your shift pattern, and enhanced annual leave on top of the standard entitlement. Full training is provided from day one; after this initial period, the role offers the flexibility to work partially or fully remotely.
Growth opportunities
This is an entry point into our analysis review team, with a clear path toward more senior roles. There's also potential to get involved in building out the automation of our analytical data processing and interpretation work, in collaboration with our software team, as the platform grows.
Location
Initial training will be based at our Glasgow site. After this, the role offers flexibility to work partially remotely.
UK right to work
Please note that the company are unable to sponsor visas for this role.

The Role
We are seeking a CADD Scientist to drive computer-aided drug design on Chemify's commercial programmes and computational platform. You will sit within a cross-disciplinary team — computational chemists, in-house and partner medicinal chemists, AI researchers, data engineers, and automation scientists — and help translate structure, simulation, and machine learning into molecules we actually make.
What sets this role apart is the design–make–test loop: working directly with partner chemists on medicinal-chemistry strategy, you will design and prioritise molecules for synthesis and see them physically made on our robotic platform within days rather than months.
If you are energised by solving complex problems at the intersection of chemistry, physics, and AI — and by seeing your designs synthesised and tested in days — we'd love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
- Run computational design across the CADD stack — docking, pharmacophore, shape and 3D-similarity, MD, FEP, and QSAR — choosing appropriate physics- and ML-based approaches for each question.
- Design, enumerate, and prioritise molecules and libraries for synthesis, and triage and analyse the results across DMTL cycles.
- Work with in-house and partner chemists on MPO, translating SAR and diverse assay readouts into actionable, biologically relevant design hypotheses.
- Communicate computational reasoning, trade-offs, and recommendations clearly to working chemists and project leads.
- Apply modern deep learning for molecular design (GNNs, generative models, property prediction) where it complements traditional CADD methods.
- Contribute to productionising CADD methods into a reproducible, API-first toolkit; partner with Infrastructure on cost-effective GPU/HPC workflows.
- Own the computational design strategy on assigned programmes from hit discovery through lead optimisation; mentor junior CADD scientists, partner with the Head of Advanced Machine Learning on growth, and act as the scientific interface with customers.

- Working knowledge of modern deep learning for molecular design (GNNs, generative models, property prediction), and a clear sense of when these complement traditional CADD methods rather than replace them.
- (Senior level) A track record of owning the computational strategy on active programmes, and of technical leadership — mentoring and influencing scientific direction beyond your own projects.
Beneficial Skills
- Hands-on experience with free energy perturbation (FEP+, OpenFE, or equivalent) in a production drug-discovery setting.
- Practical use of generative chemistry methods (diffusion, autoregressive, RL-based design), including a clear-eyed view of their failure modes.
- Familiarity with active learning, iterative DMTL design loops, and Bayesian optimisation applied to molecular design.
- Experience building or integrating CADD tooling into API-first platforms (FastAPI, Docker, CI/CD), and proficiency in C/C++ / CUDA for high-performance computational chemistry.
- A visible track record in the field — peer-reviewed publications, open-source contributions, or public projects that demonstrate your judgement on real CADD problems.

Reporting to the Head of Advanced Machine Learning, you will shape the computational platform behind every project at Chemify.

We are a Series B deep-tech company investing in world-class infrastructure and tackling problems at the frontier of AI, robotics, and chemistry. You will have the resources, the data, and the mandate to do CADD in a way that isn't possible elsewhere.
